data.name: Tabs_Settings_AppearanceLockedHint
data.value: Pause the simulation to change display mode, mesh and textures

data.name: Tabs_Settings_NoMeshesHint
data.value: Import a mesh in the Imports tab to use it here

data.name: Tabs_Model_JetNeverLit
data.value: This site is never lit between {0} and {1}: the jet emits no dust. Move it to another latitude, or change the range.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_Step1Help
data.value: Type a comet name or designation (for example 67P) and press Search.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_Step2Help
data.value: Select the comet in the results, then one of its ephemeris (SPK) records.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_Step3Help
data.value: Enter the start and end epochs to simulate (at least 1 day), or use Model range below.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_Step4Help
data.value: Choose the reference orbit and press Download & Commit (or Recommit after a range edit).

data.name: Tabs_Comet_StepsDoneHelp
data.value: Committed: press Play in the Timeline tab. Edit the range here to recommit.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_TipReferenceOrbit
data.value: The two-body reference orbit drawn next to the true SPK path. Required before the first commit; fixed while a comet is committed.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_TipPoleRa
data.value: Right ascension of the spin axis (J2000), in degrees.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_TipPoleDec
data.value: Declination of the spin axis (J2000), in degrees.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_TipPrimeMeridian
data.value: Rotation angle of the nucleus at J2000, in degrees: it sets which side faces where at a given time.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_TipRotPeriod
data.value: Sidereal rotation period in hours. It also sets the length of one rotation in Model range.

data.name: Tabs_Imports_Hint
data.value: Meshes: OBJ, PLY, glTF, GLB · Textures: PNG, JPEG, KTX2. Textures embedded in a mesh are listed separately.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_BillboardsHint
data.value: Show an imported texture in its own window over the desktop. Drag it with the left button; right click cycles the move, rotate and scale handles, which you drag with the right button (Ctrl snaps the rotation, Shift keeps the aspect).

data.name: Tabs_Settings_BillboardsNoTextures
data.value: Import a PNG, JPEG or uncompressed KTX2 texture in the Imports tab first.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_BillboardMissing
data.value: Texture not loaded: import it again to show it.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_InputBindingsHint
data.value: Rebind captures the next key chord (Esc cancels). Changes apply at once and are saved.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_PropagateDetailHint
data.value: Size steps whose orbits are solved exactly per frame; the rest are interpolated. Lower: faster, dust tails a little straighter

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HazeDetailHint
data.value: Packets per dust cluster when the haze is drawn on the coarsest level. Lower: faster, the haze's light sampled more coarsely

data.name: Tabs_Settings_ReuseToleranceHint
data.value: Reuses dust that moved less than this many pixels instead of drawing it again. Off draws every frame fresh; higher values are faster but can smear moving dust.

data.name: ModeBar_OrbitTip
data.value: Orbit viewer: the comet's orbit in the Solar System, animated over the chosen interval

data.name: ModeBar_NucleusTip
data.value: Nucleus: orientation, Sun direction, illumination and active areas

data.name: ModeBar_ModelTip
data.value: Model: compare with the telescope image; the end date is the image date, the start date the chosen number of rotations earlier

data.name: ModeBar_NoFitsHint
data.value: Import a FITS image to set the model's dates from it

data.name: Billboard_PxRatio_AtComet
data.value: orthographic: the angle at the comet's distance

data.name: Billboard_PxRatio_Tip
data.value: How many viewport pixels one image pixel covers at the viewport's current zoom and size: the image's arcsec per px divided by the viewport centre pixel's arcsec per px (vertical field of view ÷ viewport height px). At 1.0 the model and the telescope image are compared at the same scale.

data.name: Ephemeris_Tip
data.value: Geocentric astrometric ephemeris of the committed comet at the shown epoch (light-time corrected, no aberration), as in a JPL Horizons observer table. Sun PA is Horizons' PsAng: the position angle of the extended Sun→comet vector on the sky, from north through east; a tail points near it.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpSpkRecords
data.value:
Ephemeris (SPK) records of the selected comet: each is a separate fit of its orbit.
Select one, then press Download & Commit to attach it to the simulation.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpEpochRange
data.value:
Start and End of the simulated period, as ISO 8601 dates (e.g. 2000-01-01T12:00:00Z), in the time scale shown in the labels (Settings › Time scale for dates; UTC by default).
The period must be at least 1 day long: End at least 1 day after Start.
Typing here only proposes a range; Download & Commit (or Recommit) applies it.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpProposedRange
data.value:
The range in the Start/End boxes: what the next Download & Commit or Recommit will use.
It does not change the running simulation. Restore puts the committed range back in the boxes.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpRecommit
data.value:
Commits the comet again (as Download & Commit) with the range in the boxes. The dust restarts from the new start.
Until then the simulation keeps the committed range.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpModelRange
data.value:
A range for the comparison with a telescope image (the Model view): it ends at the image epoch and starts N full nucleus rotations earlier, so the simulated dust history covers N full spins before the image.
Rotations: N, a whole number of at least 1. One rotation lasts the rotation period (Rotational Model: 360° divided by the rotation rate).
Ending at: normally the epoch of your telescope image (the FITS "Model range" button fills it with the observation epoch). Leave it empty to use the End box.
Set range: sets Start and End (N × period, never less than 1 day). It only proposes the range: Download & Commit applies it.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpDustLead
data.value:
Days the jets start emitting before the start epoch, from 0 to 30 (30 = one dust lifetime, the default).
With 30 the tail is already fully formed when the timeline starts; with 0 the jets switch on at the start and the tail grows from nothing.
Used the next time the comet is committed.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpReferenceOrbit
data.value:
The red track is a two-body (Keplerian) reference orbit drawn next to the true SPK path.
SBDB solution: the elements JPL publishes, osculating at the solution epoch, which can be years away from your window (67P: 2015-10-10, about 0.12 AU off its 2025 path because of Jupiter).
Osculating at start epoch: elements recomputed from the SPK position and velocity at your start epoch. Exact there, and within about 10³ km over a month (planetary perturbations and outgassing forces).
Required before the first commit; it cannot be changed while a comet is committed.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpNucleusRadius
data.value:
Bounding-sphere radius of the comet nucleus, in km (0.1 to 100); the jets start on this sphere.
Auto-filled from Horizons when a comet is committed. Override it here if needed.
An edit after Play returns the simulation to the snapshot taken at Play.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpPoleRa
data.value:
Right ascension of the spin axis (J2000), in degrees.
With Pole Dec it sets where the spin axis points on the sky. These are not rotations: the nucleus rotates only about its own axis, and the axis stays fixed in space; RA/Dec only orient it.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpPoleDec
data.value:
Declination of the spin axis (J2000), in degrees.
With Pole RA it sets where the spin axis points on the sky. These are not rotations: the nucleus rotates only about its own axis, and the axis stays fixed in space; RA/Dec only orient it.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpPrimeMeridian
data.value:
The nucleus' rotation angle at the reference date J2000, in degrees (where longitude 0 faces).
It sets which side faces where at a given time, i.e. the timing of the jet spirals, not the outline of the fan.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpRotPeriod
data.value:
Sidereal rotation period, in hours. It edits the rotation rate in the Advanced expander (°/day); the sign (prograde/retrograde) is kept. Example: 718 °/day = 12.03 h.
It also sets the length of one rotation in Model range.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpRatesAdvanced
data.value:
RA Rate and Dec Rate: slow drift of the spin axis right ascension and declination (precession), in degrees per Julian century. 0, the default, keeps the axis fixed.
Rotation Rate: the nucleus spin in degrees per day (the IAU rotation rate W), the same spin as the period: period (h) = 360 × 24 / |rate|. The sign gives prograde (+) or retrograde (−) spin.

data.name: Tabs_Comet_HelpBodyFixed
data.value:
Yes: a camera attached to the nucleus turns with it, so the nucleus surface stays fixed in the view.
No: the spin is compensated, so the view keeps its direction relative to the stars while the nucleus rotates.

data.name: Tabs_Timeline_HelpEpochRange
data.value:
Start and End of the simulated period: the committed one (before a commit, the range proposed in the Comet tab), in the time scale shown in the labels (Settings › Time scale for dates).
Read-only here: change it in the Comet tab (step 3), then Download & Commit there.

data.name: Tabs_Timeline_HelpCommittedRange
data.value: The range the simulation runs: the comet's ephemeris covers it, and Play, Reset, Run to End and Go stay inside it.

data.name: Tabs_Timeline_HelpSpeed
data.value: How fast simulated time runs while playing, as simulated time per real second (for example 1 h/s: one simulated hour per second).

data.name: Tabs_Timeline_HelpPlayback
data.value:
Reset: back to the start epoch of the committed range; the dust is rebuilt there.
Play / Pause: simulated time runs at the chosen speed and the dust is computed frame by frame, so the tail evolves while you watch. Pause keeps the current epoch.
Run to End: jumps to the end epoch without animating. The dust there is rebuilt at once, so it can look complete sooner than while playing.

data.name: Tabs_Timeline_HelpCurrentEpoch
data.value:
The simulation's current epoch, in the time scale shown in the label.
Type an epoch inside the committed range and press Enter, or Go, to jump there; the dust is rebuilt at that epoch.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpSun
data.value:
Sun–comet geometry: the comet's distance from the Sun (AU), the subsolar latitude, STO (the Sun–target–observer phase angle) and the Sun's position angle (PA), in degrees.
Legacy panel, disabled: the engine now computes these from the JPL Horizons SPK ephemerides along the epoch timeline, so they need no manual input.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpShowReferenceError
data.value:
Draws two lines from the comet to its reference orbit (the red track): • cross-track: to the closest point of the track; • same-epoch: to where the reference says the comet should be now.
Each line is shown only while it is longer than 10 nucleus radii.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustVisibility
data.value:
Display stretch of the dust: the softening of an asinh curve over the accumulated optical depth, relative to the brightest dust in view (it adapts to the view like an eye). From 0.00001 to 1, on a logarithmic scale.
Smaller: the faint, old tail and trail (thousands of times fainter than the coma) become visible while the coma saturates. 1: close to linear, physically proportional brightness.
Visual only: the simulated dust is unchanged.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustFlow
data.value:
Brightness marks riding the dust along synchrones (the dust of one emission instant), a motion cue near the nucleus: peak 4×, trough 0.15×, mean 1.
Off by default: seen from 0.03 AU and beyond, the marks are the synchrone fan itself, hard rays through the nucleus that the physical optical depth does not show.
Visual only. Their speed is set by the flow time-lapse.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustRhoNorm
data.value:
Divides the dust brightness by the distance from the nucleus (ρ), so the bright inner coma and the faint outer jets share one exposure.
Display only: the simulated dust is unchanged.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustTrajectories
data.value: Draws as lines the paths of about 200 grains since they left the nucleus, one colour per jet.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustExposure
data.value: Brightens (+) or darkens (−) the dust over the automatic exposure, in photographic stops (EV), from −6 to +6 in steps of 0.25. One stop doubles or halves the brightness.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustTracers
data.value:
Draws one dust cluster in 256 as bright dots at the exact positions of its grain sizes, from the slow large grains to the fast small ones: the dots span the tail.
The dust drifts at 2 to 150 m/s while a pixel of a wide view spans tens of km: at low simulation speed it moves far less than a pixel per second, and the dense dots blend into a still fog. Tracers are real particles to follow (raise the simulation speed to see them stream).
Visual only.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustFlowSpeed
data.value:
Speed of the brightness marks (flow pulses) that ride the dust while the simulation runs; they freeze on pause. From 1 to 10000, on a logarithmic scale.
1: the marks move exactly with the dust (its real speed on screen, often far below a pixel per second in wide views). K: every mark moves K times faster than its dust, in its direction, so the whole swarm keeps its true velocity field at a readable pace. Changing it never jumps the marks.
Visual only.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpGizmo
Tabs_Model_HelpJetAngles
data.value: Draws the selected jet's latitude and longitude in the viewport as arcs, with their values in degrees. Saved with the file.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetLatitude
data.value: Latitude of the jet source on the nucleus, in degrees in the body-fixed frame: +90 is the north spin pole, 0 the equator, −90 the south pole.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetLongitude
data.value: Longitude of the jet source on the nucleus, in degrees from the prime meridian (−180 to 180). The nucleus spin carries the jet around as it rotates.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetStreamColor
data.value:
Colour used to draw this jet in the viewport (its dust and direction line).
Display only: it does not change the physics.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetBeta
data.value:
Computed, read-only. β is the ratio of the solar radiation-pressure force to solar gravity on the reference grain: β ≈ 0.57 · Q_pr / (ρ · s), with ρ the density in g/cm³ and s the grain radius in µm.
Small, light grains have a larger β and curve away from the Sun faster.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetQDust
data.value: Computed, read-only. The dust mass production rate at 1 AU from the Sun, in kg/s, as the engine applies it: this jet's Q_d at 1 AU clamped to the model-wide max (Q_d max).

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetDiameter
data.value:
Reference grain diameter of this jet, in µm. With density and Q_pr it sets β, the radiation-pressure push: smaller or lighter grains curve away from the Sun faster.
The size law spans radii from s₀/F to s₀·F around s₀, half the diameter.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetDensity
data.value: Bulk density of this jet's grains, in g/cm³ (cometary dust about 0.5 to 1). It enters β and the dust mass a given brightness needs.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetQpr
data.value: Radiation-pressure efficiency Q_pr of this jet's grains (0.5 to 2; 1 is a grey body). It scales β only, not the brightness.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetAlbedo
data.value: Geometric albedo of this jet's dust (0.01 to 0.5; cometary dust 0.03 to 0.06). It scales the brightness only; the amount of dust is the jet's production rate Q_d.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetSizeQ
data.value:
Exponent q of this jet's grain size law n(s) ∝ s^−q (2 to 5; 3.5 is the usual value). A larger q means more small grains.
Limitation: q only changes the individual bright specks; the continuous dust rendering assumes q = 3.5.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetSizeRange
data.value: Range factor F of this jet's grains (1 to 1000): radii span from s₀/F to s₀·F, where s₀ is half the diameter. A larger F means a wider spread of grain sizes.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetGrain
data.value:
This jet's own dust grains: every jet has its own, and a new jet starts from the defaults further down.
Grain radii follow n(s) ∝ s^−q from s₀/F to s₀·F, s₀ = diameter/2 (q = 3.5, F = 10, 100 µm → radii 5–500 µm).
Diameter, density and Q_pr set β ∝ Q_pr/(ρ·s), how hard sunlight pushes the grains away from the Sun. The albedo sets how bright they are; the amount of dust is the jet's production rate Q_d (Advanced: activity).
Each field has its own ? with its range.
Limitation: q only changes the individual bright specks; the continuous dust rendering is built for q = 3.5 whatever q is.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetActivity
data.value:
This jet's dust mass production rate Q_d at 1 AU from the Sun, in kg/s: how much dust it produces. The jets add up: the comet's total is the Σ read-out under Advanced: activity (Q_d) in the defaults.
Q_d(r) = min(max, Q_d₀ · r^−k), zero beyond the cutoff; the exponent k, the cutoff and the max are shared by every jet (Advanced: activity (Q_d) under Defaults for new jets).
Q_d does not depend on the grain (density, size, albedo) or the speed: those set the brightness and β only.
Comets range from well under 1 kg/s to thousands of kg/s.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetDustRate0
data.value:
This jet's dust mass production rate at 1 AU from the Sun, in kg/s. It scales as r_h^−k up to the max and stops beyond the cutoff (both shared by every jet).
Comets range from well under 1 kg/s to thousands of kg/s.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpCopyGrain
data.value:
Gives every other jet this jet's grain and activity: diameter, density, Q_pr, albedo, q, F and Q_d₀.
Their sites, speeds and colours stay as they are.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpJetDefaults
data.value:
Every jet has its own grain (diameter, density, Q_pr, albedo, q, F) and its own Q_d₀: edit them in the selected jet's Grain and Activity panels.
The values here are what a newly added jet starts from; changing them does not change existing jets. Only the shape of the Q_d law (exponent, cutoff, max, under Advanced: activity) is shared by every jet.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustDensity
data.value:
Bulk density of the grains of new jets, in g/cm³ (cometary dust about 0.5 to 1). It enters β and the dust mass a given brightness needs.
Each jet then has its own (its Grain panel).

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustDiameter
data.value:
Reference grain diameter of new jets, in µm. With density and Q_pr it sets β, the radiation-pressure push: smaller or lighter grains curve away from the Sun faster.
Each jet then has its own (its Grain panel).

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpScatteringEfficiency
data.value:
Radiation-pressure efficiency Q_pr of new jets' grains (0.5 to 2; 1 is a grey body). It scales β only, not the brightness.
Each jet then has its own (its Grain panel).

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustAlbedo
data.value:
Geometric albedo of new jets' dust (0.01 to 0.5; cometary dust 0.03 to 0.06). It scales the brightness only, not the production rate Q_d.
Each jet then has its own (its Grain panel).

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpActivity
data.value:
Q_d is the dust mass production rate: how much dust (kg/s) the comet produces at each distance from the Sun.
Q_d(r) = min(max, Q_d₀ · r^−k), zero beyond the cutoff. • Q_d at 1 AU: the rate at 1 AU (kg/s), per jet; the value here is the default for new jets. • Exponent k: how fast the rate falls with solar distance (k = 2: twice as far → 4× less dust). • Cutoff: distance where the emission stops. • Max: cap on the rate close to the Sun. k, cutoff and max are shared by every jet.
The Σ line at the top is the comet's total activity: the jets' rates Q_d add up. It is shown at 1 AU from the Sun and, with a committed comet, at its current distance.
Q_d sets the amount of dust directly: it does not depend on the grain or the speed. Density, diameter and albedo set how bright that dust is and how hard radiation pressure pushes the grains (β ∝ 1/(ρ·s)), i.e. how much the coma curves away from the Sun.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustRate0
data.value:
Default dust mass production rate at 1 AU from the Sun for new jets, in kg/s. It scales as r_h^−k up to the max and stops beyond the cutoff.
Each jet then has its own (its Activity panel).

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustRatePower
data.value:
Exponent k of the production law Q_d(r) = Q_d₀ · r^−k, with r the distance from the Sun in AU (1 to 4). 2 is the classic value; a larger k means the rate drops faster as the comet recedes.
Shared by every jet.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustRateCutoff
data.value:
Distance from the Sun, in AU (3 to 100), beyond which the comet emits no dust.
Shared by every jet.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpDustRateMax
data.value:
Upper limit on each jet's dust production rate, in kg/s, so that the emission does not grow without bound close to the Sun.
Shared by every jet.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpSizeDistribution
data.value:
The size range new jets start from. The exponent q is set per jet, in each jet's Grain panel (new jets start at q = 3.5).
Grain radii follow n(s) ∝ s^−q from s₀/F to s₀·F, s₀ = diameter/2 (q = 3.5, F = 10, 100 µm → radii 5–500 µm).
By number, small grains dominate; by cross-section (what sets brightness) the law is s^(2−q), so brightness favours small grains only slowly.
The continuous dust rendering is built for q = 3.5; changing q only affects the individual bright specks.

data.name: Tabs_Model_HelpSizeRange
data.value:
Default range factor F for new jets (1 to 1000): grain radii span from s₀/F to s₀·F, where s₀ is half the reference diameter. A larger F means a wider spread of grain sizes.
Each jet then has its own (its Grain panel).

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpDisplayMode
data.value:
Default: draws the nucleus as a plain procedural sphere of the nucleus radius.
Custom mesh: draws an imported 3D mesh with its textures, chosen below (import meshes in the Imports tab).
Appearance only: the simulation is unaffected. The choice locks while the simulation plays.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpMesh
data.value:
Imported 3D mesh used to draw the nucleus. Import meshes in the Imports tab.
Appearance only: the simulation is unaffected.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpChannelAlbedo
data.value:
Texture for the albedo channel: the base colour and reflectivity of the nucleus surface.
Appearance only.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpChannelNormal
data.value:
Texture for the normal channel: fine surface relief (bumps and slopes) used for shading.
Appearance only.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpChannelRoughness
data.value:
Texture for the roughness channel: how matte (rough) or glossy each point of the surface is.
Appearance only.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpChannelAo
data.value:
Texture for the ambient occlusion channel: darkens crevices that receive less scattered light.
Appearance only.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpBillboardTexture
data.value: Imported texture to show in a new billboard window over the desktop; the button next to it opens the window. Import images in the Imports tab.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpBillboardAspectLock
data.value: When on, changing the width or height also changes the other, keeping the image proportions.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpBillboardAlpha
data.value: Opacity of the billboard, from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque).

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpBillboardRotation
data.value: Rotation of the billboard about its centre, in degrees (−180 to 180). The rotation handle on the billboard does the same.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpImageHeightKm
data.value:
The image's vertical extent at the comet, in kilometres (dot decimals), for an image without a WCS (a JPEG, for example). When set, it wins over the plate scale.
Empty: not set.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpPlateScale
data.value:
The image's plate scale, in arcseconds per image pixel (dot decimals). A FITS image fills it from its WCS. The image height at the comet, when set, wins over it.
Empty: not set.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpHeaderNucleusPixel
data.value: Nucleus pixel (image px: x right, y down, pixel centres at whole numbers)

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpNucleusPixel
data.value:
Where the comet's nucleus is in the image, in image pixels: x is the column from the left, y the row from the top; the centre of the first column and of the first row is 0. 'Center on comet' puts this point on the comet.
Empty: the image centre.
Detect finds the nucleus: the brightest 9 × 9 px spot in the central third of the image, refined to the brightness-weighted centre within 12 px (a FITS image is measured on its data, not on the stretch).

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpPhysicalSize
data.value:
Sizes and places the billboard like the sky its image covers, for the Earth observer.
Apply physical size: sizes the billboard to the sky its image covers at the Earth observer's current scale, and keeps it so on zoom and resize (a manual resize unbinds it).
Center on comet: moves the billboard so its nucleus pixel (the image centre when unset) lies on the comet as the viewport draws it, keeping its size and rotation. Enabled while the comet is on screen.
Match camera to image: aims the Earth observer at the comet and sets its field so the viewport's height shows the image's height (km, or plate scale × image height); the billboard fills the viewport's height, centred on the comet.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpFlipLon
data.value: Uses the opposite sign of the site longitude: some headers say 'west' for an east-positive value (the Liverpool Telescope's LONGITUD). The header's LST settles it when present.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpStretch
data.value:
How the FITS data values map to black and white.
Mode: ZScale is IRAF zscale (the import's default); Percentile puts black and white at two percentiles; Manual puts them at two values in data units.
Curve: the transfer curve between black and white, linear, log or asinh (brings out faint dust).
The two values (dot decimals): the low and high percentile in % in Percentile mode, the black and white points in data units in Manual mode.
Apply stretch re-renders the image.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpCompare
data.value:
Model range: puts this observation's epoch (mid-exposure, else DATE-OBS) in the Timeline tab's "rotations ending at" box and sets Start/End to N nucleus rotations ending there (at least 1 day). It only proposes the range: commit it in the Comet tab, or use Recommit in the Timeline tab.
Orient to image (Earth observer only): looks at the image centre (WCS), turns the billboard like the sky in the view and moves it to the viewport centre.
Match camera to image (Earth observer only): aims at the comet and fits the image's field (its WCS plate scale × height) to the viewport's height; the billboard fills it, centred on the comet.
Set up comparison: enters the Earth observer, then seeks, uses the site, matches the field, orients, centres the billboard and locks the viewport for comparison.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpDustQuality
data.value:
Dust drawing quality, from 1 (lowest, fastest) to 5 (ultra). Each step draws the dust finer and costs more GPU time.
Moving the slider presets the four detail settings below (volume, trajectory, haze and temporal reuse). Editing one of them by hand turns the quality to Custom.
Saved for the next start.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpVolumeDetail
data.value:
Detail of the volumetric dust. Lower values are faster but draw it more coarsely; higher values are finer and cost more GPU time.
Set by the Quality preset; saved for the next start.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpPropagateDetail
data.value:
Number of grain-size steps whose orbits are solved exactly each frame; the sizes in between are interpolated.
Lower is faster, with dust tails a little straighter.
Set by the Quality preset; saved for the next start.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpHazeDetail
data.value:
Packets per dust cluster when the haze is drawn at its coarsest level.
Lower is faster, with the light of the haze sampled more coarsely.
Set by the Quality preset; saved for the next start.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpReuseTolerance
data.value:
Dust that moved less than this many screen pixels is reused instead of being drawn again (Off, or 1 to 16 px).
Off redraws every frame fresh; higher values are faster but can smear moving dust.
Set by the Quality preset; saved for the next start.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewDiagnostics
data.value:
Shows the camera coordinates, dust history, observer line and orbit debug panels over the viewport, in all viewports at once.
For checking the engine; hidden by default.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewComparisonLock
data.value:
Refuses mouse orbit, pan and zoom and greys out the projection settings, so the view stays matched to a telescope image.
Turn it off to move the camera again.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewProjectionType
data.value:
Perspective: distant objects look smaller, like a camera. The field of view sets the zoom.
Orthographic: no perspective, the size of an object does not depend on its distance (like a map or a flat telescope image). The half-width and half-height set what is visible.
The parameters of both are under Advanced: projection.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewProjectionAdvanced
data.value:
The field of view (perspective) or the half-width and half-height (orthographic), the near and far clip planes and the units they are shown in.
A billboard's Match camera to image sets the field from the image instead.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewFov
data.value:
Vertical field of view of the perspective camera, in the unit chosen in Units below.
Smaller values zoom in; telescope fields are measured in arcminutes.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewFovUnits
data.value:
Unit of the field of view: degrees, arcminutes (1/60 degree) or arcseconds (1/3600 degree).
Only changes the display: the field itself stays the same.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewPerspNear
data.value:
Objects closer to the camera than this distance are not drawn.
Shown in the distance units below.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewPerspFar
data.value:
Objects farther from the camera than this distance are not drawn.
Shown in the distance units below.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewDistanceUnits
data.value:
Unit used to show the clip-plane distances: AU, km or m.
Only changes the display; the values are stored in AU.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewHalfWidth
data.value: Half of the visible width of the orthographic view, in the chosen units: the view spans plus or minus this value around its centre.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewHalfHeight
data.value: Half of the visible height of the orthographic view, in the chosen units: the view spans plus or minus this value around its centre.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewOrthoUnits
data.value:
Unit used to show the half-width, the half-height and the clip planes: AU, km or m.
Only changes the display; the values are stored in AU.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewOrthoNear
data.value: Nearest distance along the view direction that is drawn, in the chosen units. Anything closer is not drawn.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewOrthoFar
data.value: Farthest distance along the view direction that is drawn, in the chosen units. Anything farther is not drawn.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewProportionsLock
data.value:
Keeps the half-width to half-height ratio equal to the viewport's shape, also when the window is resized, so the image is never stretched.
Restore Proportions recomputes the half-width from the half-height once.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewShowBehindCamera
data.value:
Orthographic only: also draws the geometry behind the camera plane (within the far distance), as a telescope image does.
Dust behind the camera is not drawn. A perspective view cannot show it.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewPhysicalLighting
data.value:
Direct sunlight only, scaled with the comet's heliocentric distance r as (1 AU / r)², and exposed so that a white surface facing the Sun at 1 AU is drawn white. No ambient fill.
The surface the Sun does not reach is drawn in dark indigo.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewNucleusFromEarth
data.value: Switches to the Earth observer tracking the comet, celestial north up, with a field a few nucleus diameters tall: the nucleus lit by the Sun as seen from Earth.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpViewNucleusExposure
data.value:
Brightness of the sunlit nucleus, in stops (EV): each whole step doubles or halves it; the slider moves in half stops.
At 0 a white surface facing the Sun is drawn white.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpObserverTopocentric
data.value:
On (topocentric): the observer stands at the telescope site on the Earth's surface (latitude and longitude below) and turns with the Earth. This shifts the apparent position of nearby objects by diurnal parallax and adds a horizon.
Off (geocentric): the camera is at the Earth's centre and only follows its motion around the Sun.
The view never rotates with the Earth. Saved with the file.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpObserverNorthUp
data.value:
On: the view is levelled to celestial north (J2000), north up and east left, like a telescope image.
Off: levelled to the ecliptic pole (on the site's side of the equator).
Saved with the file.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpObserverLatitude
data.value: Latitude of the observing site in degrees, positive north of the equator (−90 to 90). Used by the topocentric observer.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpObserverLongitude
data.value: Longitude of the observing site in degrees, positive east of Greenwich (−180 to 180). Used by the topocentric observer.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpObserverLookDirection
data.value:
Free look: drag to look around; the direction stays fixed among the stars.
Comet tracking: keeps the comet exactly at the centre of the view.
Sun tracking: keeps the Sun at the centre of the view.
From the surface, while the tracked target is below the horizon, the view faces the horizon where it will rise.
Restore preset projection re-applies the tracking projection where the target spans 10% of the view.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpObserverScale
data.value: The angle one screen pixel covers and the field of view; at the comet's distance also the kilometres per pixel and the half-width and half-height of the view.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_PlayPreviewHint
data.value: How the dust is drawn while playing and for 2 s after a pause or a seek: coarser and fresh every frame, with moving flow marks. The full render follows.

data.name: Tabs_Settings_HelpPlayPreview
data.value:
While the simulation plays, and for 2 s after a pause or a seek, the dust is drawn as a preview: coarser, redrawn every frame (no temporal reuse), with the flow marks moving out of the nucleus. The flow marks are a visual aid: they travel along the real velocity field, faster than the dust at slow speeds; the particles stay where the physics puts them.
Smooth is the fastest, Quality the finest; Off draws the full render while playing too.
When the preview ends the full render starts and refines. "Render full" on the viewport starts it at once. Saved for the next start.
